checklist.notes: the request example supports short A1.2 writing; the rubric stays tied to authorized written targets.
Draft-first states, preservation of meaning, at most three feedback priorities, revision, and no full replacement support learner ownership.
The protocol reuses a source-lesson utterance and declared scope rather than introducing an unrelated target.
Length and the example are clear, though ‘lesson-scoped’ and the desired content remain implicit.
One question at a time and bounded output or feedback keep the interaction manageable for the declared tier.
A required learner draft, target-based feedback, and a revision state are appropriate for writing tutoring.
The short, structured self-study interaction is accessible to Vietnamese learners and avoids unsupported population-wide or accent claims.

findings.description: The task requests ‘lesson-scoped sentences’ from one example but does not express its rubric targets as learner-friendly content requirements.
findings.recommendation: Replace the technical phrase with one or two plain-language requirements without supplying a full answer.

limitations: Static protocol wording only was reviewed. No live provider behavior, audio realization, learner response or outcome, provider authentication, human review, or release approval was observed or claimed.
